text: A host at 192.168.10.70/27 wants to send to 192.168.10.100. Which address does it ARP for?
explanation: With a /27 mask, .70 is in the 64-95 block and .100 is in the 96-127 block, so the destination is remote. The host ARPs for its default gateway and sends the frame there with the IP destination still set to .100. This off-subnet case is the one students most often get wrong.
